summary: OpenStreetMap is a collaborative project for creating a free, editable map of the world. It provides geographical data and mapping capabilities that you can host independently to serve your own map tiles and spatial queries.
goodFor: This is a good fit if you need to run an independent geographical mapping service without relying on commercial map providers.
watchOut: Self-hosting mapping infrastructure involves heavy resource requirements for rendering and storing large spatial datasets, which can demand significant disk space and hardware tuning.
deployNotes: As a Ruby application, it typically requires a separate database for spatial data storage, a process manager, and a reverse proxy to handle web traffic securely.
